scope: Proposition 4.8 (Closing a protected window) of the manuscript “Canonical conformal limits of subcritical FK planar maps” (preprints/Canonical-conformal-limits-of-subcritical-FK-planar-maps-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e7dab39caf778176), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 19. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Work in a bilateral contour coupling with locally uniform convergence to its peanosphere contour. Given finitely many compact spatial tests and open buffers about them, one may choose a bounded time window, and then a finite spherical tree/cotree sewing, with the following properties for all large n. (i) Every flag star needed by the tests is unchanged, including its cyclic order and all original primal incidences. (ii) On a neighborhood of these flags there are continuous projections with the conclusions of Proposition 4.2 and Lemma 4.3, and the local joining conclusion of Lemma 4.4 holds with arbitrary fixed clearance. (iii) The finite sewing admits homeomorphisms into the reference one-point compactification for which the projection error tends to zero over the tests. The inverse images of the tested compact sets are contained in the unchanged part. Consequently both directions of every strict crossing or separation test take place in the original discrete surface. The construction can be made simultaneously for a countable exhaustion of compact tests and their finite refinements, by diagonalization.
